pk.context: 10 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: Only about 20% bioavailable and barely metabolized, this statin is excreted mainly in the feces.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is about 20%, and food does not change the AUC. It is 88% bound to plasma proteins, and about 72% of body clearance after an intravenous dose is hepatic.
A calcium salt, a white amorphous powder that is sparingly soluble in water. The parent molecular weight is 481.5.
Tablets under an NDA, in 5, 10, 20 and 40 mg strengths.

Contraindicated in acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis, and in hypersensitivity to the drug or its excipients. Headache and myalgia are the adverse reactions reported most often in the table.

Reducing major adverse cardiovascular events in adults at increased risk, and as an adjunct to diet to lower LDL cholesterol in hypercholesterolemia, familial forms, dysbetalipoproteinemia and hypertriglyceridemia.
Inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme that converts HMG-CoA to mevalonate, a precursor of cholesterol.
The generic name begins with R and has twelve letters.
